title: CACLENS predicts and validates a zearalenone-degrading enzyme
summary: The multitask deep-learning enzyme-screening framework CACLENS selected ten candidate enzymes for zearalenone (ZEN) degradation, which were expressed and tested. One candidate degraded more than 90% of both ZEN and its analogue α-zearalenol (α-ZOL) in the reported assay.
ai_technology: CACLENS (Cross-Attention & Contrastive Learning-enabled Enzyme Selection), a multimodal multitask deep-learning enzyme classifier
organization: Shanghai Institute of Nutrition and Health, Chinese Academy of Sciences; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

evidence.tested: The multitask deep-learning enzyme-screening framework CACLENS selected ten candidate enzymes for zearalenone (ZEN) degradation, which were expressed and tested.
evidence.unknown: This is an in-vitro enzyme degradation finding; it does not establish safety of degradation products, remediation performance at environmental scale, or food/feed safety. The abstract does not name the successful enzyme or its degradation-product identity.
evidence.ai_role: CACLENS combined reaction-type classification, EC-number prediction and reaction-feasibility estimates to screen candidate enzymes. The paper then expressed and assayed ten selected enzyme candidates against ZEN; one showed >90% degradation of ZEN and α-ZOL.
